description: Table 1 is a single two-row chemical-composition table rendered as an image, headed "Matrix compositions of the 0Al and 1.3Al steels. (mass fraction, wt%)". The table has nine columns: the first column is the steel label ("Steel"), followed by the alloying elements C, Si, Mn, Cr, Ni, Mo, V and Al. All values are given in mass fraction (wt%) with two decimal places and no units printed inside the cells. Row 1 is steel 0Al: C 0.32, Si 1.98, Mn 1.02, Cr 1.00, Ni 3.41, Mo 0.56, V 0.09, Al 0.03. Row 2 is steel 1.3Al: C 0.31, Si 2.01, Mn 1.03, Cr 1.00, Ni 5.06, Mo 0.60, V 0.11, Al 1.30. The two rows are nearly identical except for the deliberate Al addition (0.03 → 1.30 wt%) and the accompanying increase in Ni (3.41 → 5.06 wt%), with minor variations in C, Si, Mn, Mo and V and identical Cr (1.00 wt%). The table therefore documents the two base alloys compared throughout the paper and shows that the 1.3Al heat was designed by raising Ni and Al together while keeping the remaining matrix chemistry of the 0Al reference steel essentially unchanged. No micrographs, curves or error values appear in this item.

subfigures.description: Single composition table with header row Steel, C, Si, Mn, Cr, Ni, Mo, V, Al and two data rows for steels 0Al and 1.3Al; values in mass fraction (wt%).

observations.observation: The table lists compositions in mass fraction (wt%) for two steels labelled 0Al and 1.3Al.
Cr is identical at 1.00 wt% in both steels.
Al rises from 0.03 wt% in 0Al to 1.30 wt% in 1.3Al, and Ni rises from 3.41 to 5.06 wt% over the same pair.
No units, uncertainties or measurement methods are printed inside the table cells.
The caption states Table 1 gives the matrix compositions of the 0Al and 1.3Al steels in mass fraction (wt%).
To ensure sufficient NiAl content in the 1.3Al steel, the Ni and Al concentrations were increased relative to the 0Al steel composition.
Both materials were produced by vacuum induction melting followed by vacuum arc remelting (VIM + VAR) into 500 kg ingots, then forged into billets with Φ170 mm.
Specimens for microstructural and mechanical characterization were extracted from the quarter-radius position of the billets.
The two steels are referred to as 0Al and 1.3Al in the citing text for simplicity.
